scene: the round pressure gauge of a wall boiler photographed close in a cramped hall cupboard, the needle sitting just under one on a scratched dial with a green band and a red band, condensation on the glass, a copper filling loop and a grey lever below it, a dusty skirting board and a lifted corner of carpet at the bottom of the frame, hard direct torchlight from one side and darkness behind

a printed hospital night rota for july lying on a chipped melamine counter, a grid of names and dates with two cells ringed hard in pencil and a third crossed through, the sheet creased into thirds from a pocket, a set of keys and a folded paper bag beside it, a strip-lit corridor reflection across the paper, flat bright institutional light

a deep bowl of thick orange soup on a steel kitchen bench, a swirl of oil across the surface and a scatter of black pepper, the emptied end of a marrow and a paper label with a name on it pushed to one side, a heavy pan behind with a dinner plate resting on top of it instead of a lid, one bare bulb and an open window of pale evening

an empty wire in-tray on a scuffed staff room desk, one paperclip and a curl of torn paper left in the bottom of it, a squared stack of finished school reports pushed away at the edge of the frame with a blue biro across them, a cold mug ringed inside, late afternoon sun coming in low and flat across the desk

an art room stripped for the summer, chairs upended on tables in rows, the display walls bare down to pinholes and a few strips of faded sugar paper still stapled at the corners, a plan chest with its top drawer half open, a mop bucket by the door and one window propped, harsh late light with dust in it and long shadows across a scarred lino floor

the painted iron rail of a small passenger ferry seen from the top deck, chipped white gloss over rust and a knotted length of rope on a cleat, grey green water racing past below and the mainland receding into haze, a lifebuoy bracket at the edge of the frame, cold early morning light and a smear of spray on the lens

a dry stone wall running along the top path of a small island, sheep cropped turf and thrift growing out of the gaps, a wooden stile with one worn step, the sea flat and pale beyond the drop and a single white house far off on the headland, high thin cloud and a wide bright sky with no sun in the frame

an open paper wrap of chips balanced on a harbour wall, thick cut and steaming with salt on them and a wooden fork stuck in upright, grease going translucent through the paper, a plastic bottle of vinegar and two paper napkins weighted under a stone, the harbour water and a moored dinghy out of focus behind, bright flat afternoon light

the canal from the towpath in the evening after rain, the water risen and brown and holding a broken reflection of the far bank, only the top corner of a submerged shopping trolley breaking the surface, wet cobbles and a black mooring ring in the foreground, willow leaves overhead and a warm low light going orange along the far wall

a battered steel flask and two enamel cups standing on a low stone wall at the top of a hill at dusk, one cup steaming, a folded coat and a paper bag with a corner torn off beside them, the city spread out far below in dim orange grids with a river running black through it, the last blue of the sky above and no lamp nearby

a heavy pan on a hob with a brand new glass and steel lid seated on it, steam fogging the underside of the glass and a bead of water running down, the cardboard sleeve the lid came in propped against the tiles behind, a wooden spoon on a saucer and a chopping board with onion ends, warm kitchen light and a dark window
